items.title: Stock Market Today: Dow, S&P 500 Hit New Highs; SpaceX Jumps Ahead Of Q2 Report
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 finished at record highs Tuesday, aided by slumping oil prices on fresh enthusiasm for a U.S.-Iran peace deal.  On the stock market today, Palantir Technologies zoomed up and Dell Technologies broke out of a base.  Space Exploration Technologies, known as SpaceX, surged before its quarterly report.

items.title: Analyst Makes Bold Dell Call Ahead of Earnings
items.summary: New rivals could weaken one of Dell's biggest growth engines

items.title: Dell: Record Backlogs & Surging AI Server Demand
items.summary: Driven by a massive backlog, key partnerships with top chip makers, and exceptionally strong technical tailwinds, Dell offers a rare blend of hyper-growth fundamentals coupled with a reasonable valuation.

items.title: NetApp's Buyback Is Better Funded Than It Is Big
items.summary: The margin behind its shareholder returns is earned in the stickiest corner of the business, but near the top of its one-year range it is the valuation, not the buyback, that you are underwriting.

items.title: Dell and Super Micro Rally 10%, Hewlett Packard Enterprise Climbs 6% as AI Server Stocks Surge
items.summary: AI server stocks are staging a dramatic Tuesday surge with no clean company catalyst in sight, raising the question of whether this risk-on wave has legs or sets up a painful late-session reversal.

items.title: Down 50% in The Year, Is SMCI a Buy?
items.summary: Super Micro Computer has shed half its value in a year, and now a board investigation, a $6.6 billion cash outflow, and a potential 48% upside are all pointing in different directions at once.

items.title: BTDR Stock Rallies After Landing $4.7B AI Infrastructure Contract In Norway
items.summary: The contract covers 121 megawatts of AI infrastructure at Bitdeer's Tydal campus in Norway and could expand to $8 billion if an eight-year renewal option is exercised.

items.title: Nvidia, Dell Back AI Cloud Startup Volta at $2.4 Billion Value
items.summary: (Bloomberg) -- Volta Infra Holdings Ltd., a new artificial intelligence cloud company, has raised $300 million in venture funding and secured an additional $5 billion worth of financing to help a wider mix of technology companies gain access to costly AI chips. The funding, set to be announced Tuesday, values Volta at $2.4 billion, and was co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Altimeter Capital. Nvidia Corp. and Michael Dell also participated.
